cues.en: Before electronic computers, people built mechanical computers to perform specific mathematical operations. One such machine was this, Albert Michelson's harmonic analyzer. This 19th century machine adds together cosines to create intricate patterns. Amazingly, it also does the inverse operation. It can take a pattern and reveal the cosines that when added together will approximate it. This operation is called Fourier analysis.
cues.zh: 在电子计算机出现之前，人们制造机械计算机来执行特定的数学运算。眼前这台就是其中之一：阿尔伯特·迈克尔逊（Albert Michelson）的谐波分析仪。这台19世纪的机器能将多个余弦波叠加在一起，生成复杂的图样。令人惊叹的是，它还能进行逆运算：输入一个图样，它就能反解出相加后可逼近该图样的各个余弦分量。这项运算被称为傅里叶分析，

cues.en: and is possibly the most important mathematical technique of the past 100 years. Without Fourier analysis, there would be no MP3s, JPEGs, or cell phones as we know them today. To celebrate this stunning machine and to gain a greater insight into what Fourier analysis is and how it works, I'll share in this video some history of this analyzer and then in three additional videos detail its operation.
cues.zh: 它可以说是过去100年里最重要的数学技术。没有傅里叶分析，就没有我们今天熟知的MP3、JPEG或手机。为了致敬这台精妙绝伦的机器，并深入理解傅里叶分析究竟是什么以及它是如何工作的，我将在本期视频中分享这台分析仪的历史，随后在接下来的三期视频中详解它的运作原理。

cues.en: In synthesis, I go step by step and examine the key components of the machine and how each plays its part in adding cosines. In analysis, I show you how the machine uses the same mechanical motions to find the frequency components of a signal you want to analyze. And in operation, I show the steps an operator of this machine must go through to perform these calculations.
cues.zh: 在“合成篇”中，我会逐步拆解这台机器的核心部件，展示各个部分如何协同完成余弦波叠加。在“分析篇”中，我将演示机器如何利用相同的机械运动，找出待分析信号的各个频率分量。而在“操作篇”中，我将演示操作员进行这些计算必须执行的具体步骤。

cues.en: This machine's designer, Albert Michelson, was famous for measuring the speed of light. Yet he also measured many other properties of the universe precisely, like the diameter of stars or the rigidity of the Earth. In the late 19th century, he performed Fourier analysis by hand to help resolve fine details of the light emitted by vaporized elements. He was doing an early version of Fourier transform spectroscopy. These hand calculations were laborious, so he invented this machine to automate these calculations.
cues.zh: 这台机器的设计者 Albert Michelson 因测量光速而闻名。但他还曾精确测量过宇宙的许多其他物理特性，比如恒星的直径或地球的刚度。在19世纪末，他通过手算傅里叶分析，来解析蒸发元素所发光谱的精细结构——他当时做的正是傅里叶变换光谱学的早期雏形。这些手算极其繁琐费力，因此他发明了这台机器来自动化完成计算。

cues.en: He built a prototype machine similar to this one in 1897 and then a larger prototype four times the size a year later. The machine was then commercialized by William Gartner and company. They made precision scientific instruments often designed by Michelson. In their 1904 catalog, they advertised this machine, which can add up to 20 different sinusoids, as well as a larger version that calculated with 80 sinusoids.
cues.zh: 他在1897年制造了一台与这台类似的样机，一年后又造了一台四倍大的大型样机。随后，该机器由 William Gartner 及其公司实现商业化生产。他们专门制造精密科学仪器，其中许多都是由 Michelson 设计的。在他们1904年的产品目录中，就刊登了这台可以叠加多达20个不同正弦波的机器，以及一台能计算80个正弦波的更大型版本。

cues.en: We know that in the early 20th century, Gartner sold at least four of these machines, and based on that, it seems this 20-element machine sold for around $225, and that it was likely made between 1901 and 1910. After this period, the machines are mentioned only occasionally. We found pictures of several different configurations until it made one last public appearance in an improved form at the 1933 World's Fair in the Great Hall of Science in an exhibit called
cues.zh: 我们知道在20世纪初，Gartner 至少售出了四台这样的机器，据此推测，这台20元件的机器售价约为225美元，很可能制造于1901年至1910年之间。此后，关于这些机器的记载便寥寥无几。我们找到了几种不同构型的照片，直到它以改良后的形态在1933年世博会的大科学厅最后一次公开亮相，展出在一个名为

cues.en: the magic of analysis. Our machine has an unknown history. We're not sure when it arrived here on the University of Illinois campus. We only know that for at least the last 40 years it is set in a glass case in Altgeld Hall. It's gears completely still. Join me as I bring back to life this stunning mechanical computer. I'm Bill Hammack, the engineer guy. Watch the other videos in this series, Synthesis, Analysis, and Operation.
cues.zh: “分析的魔力”的展位上。我们这台机器的身世已不可考，并不清楚它究竟是何时运抵伊利诺伊大学校园的。我们只知道，至少在过去的40年里，它一直静静地陈列在 Altgeld Hall 的玻璃柜中，齿轮彻底沉寂。现在，请随我一起唤醒这台令人叹为观止的机械计算机吧。我是“工程小子” Bill Hammack，欢迎观看本系列的后续视频：“合成篇”、“分析篇”与“操作篇”。
